title: Fixing the 3 Most Annoying Things in an Old House (Squeaks, Sticks and Drafts)
creator: Saturday Fix with Glen
description:
A squeaky door, a drawer that won't slide, and a draft under the back door. Three cheap fixes, about an hour total.

What you need:
bar of soap or paraffin wax
flathead screwdriver
hammer and a nail set
self-adhesive door sweep

Questions? Leave them below and I answer most of them on Sunday nights.

sentences.t: Morning, everybody, welcome back to the shop, or, well, today it's the hallway.
This house is about ninety years old and it has a lot of personality, which is a nice way of saying everything squeaks.
Today we're knocking out three of the most annoying little problems, and none of them should cost you more than a few bucks.
First up, this door.
Listen to that.
Every single time, and it's the bathroom, so it goes off at three in the morning too.
Now growing up, my dad had one answer to every squeak in the house, and it was a can of WD-40.
He'd spray it on everything, hinges, bike chains, the lawnmower, I think once on a squeaky chair he was sitting in.
And it works for a few days, but on hinges it tends to attract dust and the squeak comes right back.
So what I do instead is pull the hinge pin and put something a little thicker on it.
Close the door so the weight's off the hinges, then put a nail set under the pin and tap it up from the bottom.
There it comes, and look at that, it's dry and kind of rusty, no wonder it's complaining.
Wipe it down with a rag, a little steel wool if it's really rusty.
Then I just rub a plain bar of soap on it, the old fashioned way, or you can use a bit of white lithium grease.
Tap it back in, swing the door a few times to work it in.
Nothing, total silence, beautiful.
Okay, problem number two, this dresser drawer.
It sticks about halfway, and you have to kind of jiggle it, and it drives my wife absolutely nuts.
Old furniture like this has wooden runners, no metal slides, so it's wood rubbing on wood.
Pull the drawer all the way out and look at the bottom edges, you'll see where it's shiny, that's where it's rubbing.
Same trick as the hinge, believe it or not, rub a candle or a block of paraffin wax along the runners.
Both on the drawer and on the frame inside, really get it in there.
If the wood is swollen, which happens in summer, you might need to take a few passes with sandpaper first.
But let's try just the wax.
Look at that, it just glides now, that took about three minutes.
Last one, and this is the one that actually saves you money, the draft under the back door.
Put your hand down here, you can feel it, there's like a half inch gap at the bottom.
In January this is basically an open window.
The cheapest fix is a self-adhesive door sweep, it's a strip of rubber or brush that sticks to the bottom of the door.
Measure the width of your door, and cut the sweep about an eighth of an inch shorter so it doesn't catch the frame.
Clean the bottom of the door really well first, or the adhesive won't hold, I learned that one the hard way.
Line it up so the rubber just kisses the threshold when the door's closed, peel, and press.
Now let's check, hand down at the bottom again, and nothing, no air at all.
So that's three fixes, under an hour, and maybe ten bucks total.
If you've got an old house problem that's driving you crazy, put it in the comments and I might tackle it in a future episode.
See you next Saturday.
